fusion_only.description: Fused child interning, canonical-list construction, and hash calculation; always rebuild lists and enclosing nodes

fusion_and_reuse.pr_status: reverted from PR branch by debed4e7a9432bed84a939ac14a6cf46008ac22f

no_write_invokes_interning.evidence: No-write profile commands omit --cache_checked_modules yet report intern_decls and intern_index counters.

original_vs_fusion_profiles.note: Intrusive profiles; allocation and GC counters are whole-process.

cross_build_fusion_and_combined_profiles.note: Fusion-only and combined binaries were built in different worktrees/build rounds with materially different baselines. These counters are listed for context only and cannot isolate the incremental effect of node reuse.

adapter_allocation_analysis.original: Each child produces a hashed-result record; List.map also creates an intermediate cons cell retaining that record, followed by a canonical-value cons cell.
adapter_allocation_analysis.fusion: Each child still produces a hashed-result record; the callback additionally returns a (canonical value, hash) tuple, and intern_list creates the canonical-value cons cell.
adapter_allocation_analysis.interpretation: The new tuple adapter replaces the eliminated intermediate cons allocation with another similarly sized short-lived block. This explains why fused traversal removes traversals but barely changes whole-process allocation.

artifact_validation.comparison_note: Generic Marshal comparison checks stage 1, stage2.tc_res (including stored index), and declarations while ignoring stage2 dependency digests, which legitimately differ because compiler-specific child checked files have different byte digests.

conclusion.node_reuse_incremental_effect: not isolated because combined and fusion-only evidence comes from different compiler builds
conclusion.interpretation: Fusion-only already shows small synthetic total-time increases despite unchanged/lower pass counters. Cross-build combined counters show no consistent pass-time pattern but cannot measure reuse incrementally. The large earlier combined total-time result cannot be assigned to reuse; binary/GC layout, solver/runtime noise, or downstream phase perturbation remain possible.
